skill.name: structural-search
skill.description: Search code by AST structure with ast-grep patterns for safer, more precise code discovery and refactoring.
skill.summary: Use ast-grep structural search to find code patterns, review matches, and prepare refactors across languages.
skill.author: 0xDarkMatter

security_audit.summary: All static findings were adjudicated as false positives because they are Markdown or YAML examples for ast-grep searches, not active code executed by the skill. The skill does encourage local Bash use of ast-grep and optional rewrite commands, so users should preview matches before applying changes.

remediation.issue: Examples include commands that can modify files when rewrite flags are used.
remediation.suggestion: Keep preview-first guidance prominent and require explicit approval before running rewrite or fix commands.

remediation.issue: Shell pipeline examples with xargs may be copied into diverse repositories.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer safer examples that handle unusual filenames, such as null-delimited pipelines where practical.

content.user_title: Find Code Patterns with AST Search
content.value_statement: Text search misses semantic code patterns and creates noisy results. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to use ast-grep for precise structural search and refactoring prep.
actual_capabilities: Provides ast-grep command patterns for JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Go, and Rust.
Explains metavariables for matching identifiers, nodes, and repeated syntax.
Shows how to find function calls, imports, hooks, async code, and error handling patterns.
Includes examples for previewing and applying ast-grep rewrites.
Documents YAML rule creation, rule testing, CI use, and editor integration.
Includes security-oriented patterns for finding risky code constructs.
limitations: Requires the ast-grep CLI to be installed in the local environment.
Search quality depends on correct language selection and valid ast-grep patterns.
Rewrite examples can modify files when users run commands with rewrite flags.
Security patterns identify candidates that still require human review.

use_cases.title: Find framework usage across a codebase
use_cases.description: Locate React hooks, imports, async functions, and other syntax patterns without relying on fragile text search.

use_cases.title: Prepare safe refactoring work
use_cases.description: Preview structural matches before changing variable declarations, logging calls, or repeated API patterns.

use_cases.title: Build custom static checks
use_cases.description: Create reusable ast-grep YAML rules for linting, CI checks, and security review workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Find a simple call pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Use structural search to find every call to console.log in this repository. Show the files and explain the pattern used.

prompt_templates.title: Search a specific language pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Find Python function definitions that match def $NAME($$$): $$$ and summarize the main files where they appear.

prompt_templates.title: Preview a refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ast-grep to preview where var declarations can become const declarations. Do not apply changes until I approve.

prompt_templates.title: Design a reusable rule
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an ast-grep YAML rule that finds innerHTML assignments in TypeScript and explain how to test it before CI use.

output_examples.input: Find all React useEffect calls with dependency arrays.
output_examples.output: The skill would suggest an ast-grep pattern for useEffect calls, run it against TypeScript files, and return matched files with concise context.

output_examples.input: Help me replace console.log with logger.info.
output_examples.output: The skill would first preview structural matches, explain the rewrite pattern, and ask before applying file changes.

output_examples.input: Create a check for risky eval calls.
output_examples.output: The skill would provide an ast-grep security pattern and describe how to review matches before treating them as confirmed issues.

best_practices: Start with read-only searches before using rewrite or fix options.
Limit searches by language or directory to reduce noise and improve speed.
Review every match before treating it as a bug or security issue.
anti_patterns: Do not run rewrite commands on the whole repository without reviewing matches first.
Do not treat ast-grep matches as confirmed vulnerabilities without context.
Do not use broad shell pipelines on untrusted file lists without understanding the command.

faq.question: What is structural search?
faq.answer: Structural search matches code syntax through the abstract syntax tree, not plain text. It can find patterns that regex often misses.

faq.question: Does this skill require extra software?
faq.answer: Yes. It expects the ast-grep command line tool, often called sg, to be installed.

faq.question: Can it edit files automatically?
faq.answer: The skill includes rewrite examples, but users should preview matches and approve changes before applying rewrites.

faq.question: Which languages are covered?
faq.answer: The references include JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Go, and Rust examples, plus general YAML rule guidance.

faq.question: Is it a security scanner?
faq.answer: It includes security search patterns, but results are candidates. A reviewer must confirm whether each match is a real issue.

faq.question: How is this different from grep?
faq.answer: grep searches text. ast-grep understands syntax, so it can match functions, imports, calls, and nested structures more precisely.
